elements.element: Customer has no exclusivity obligation under the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Section 6.1 expressly states that “the Company shall have no exclusivity ... obligation under this Agreement” and removes the restrictions on similar projects and HDI’s exclusive brand-use right.

elements.element: Customer has no sole-supplier obligation under the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Section 6.1 expressly states that “the Company shall have no ... sole-supplier obligation under this Agreement” and identifies HDI as non-exclusive.

elements.element: Any exclusivity binding Customer is limited to a defined product category.
elements.evidence: The condition is absent: the rendered clause imposes no exclusivity on Customer, so no broader product-category exclusivity exists.

elements.element: Any exclusivity binding Customer is limited to 12 months.
elements.evidence: The condition is absent: the rendered clause imposes no exclusivity on Customer, including no exclusivity lasting beyond 12 months.

elements.element: Any exclusivity binding Customer ends automatically upon Vendor’s failure to meet service levels.
elements.evidence: The condition is absent because no exclusivity is imposed; therefore, a performance-based termination mechanism is unnecessary.

elements.element: Any exclusivity binding Customer ends automatically upon Vendor’s failure to meet delivery dates.
elements.evidence: The condition is absent because no exclusivity is imposed; therefore, a delivery-based termination mechanism is unnecessary.

result.reason: The operative redline fully achieves the preferred position by expressly making HDI non-exclusive and eliminating both exclusivity and sole-supplier obligations on the Company. It also removes the specific restrictions on similar Internet projects and HDI’s exclusive right to use the Deerskin brand. The fallback is satisfied because its limitations are conditional on exclusivity existing, and the rendered clause demonstrably imposes none. The changes are confined to the exclusivity provision and do not contradict the retained Section 6.2 right.
